design: PIPELINE-V6.md (caustics v3 chunk 2: rain, windless calm)

scene.note: the verification scene is preset 1's photo and sun with wind = 0 (calm): the background is the Cox-Munk floor sigma2 ~ 0.003, never a perfect mirror (PIPELINE-V6 section 7)
scene.patch_note: PIPELINE-V6 section 7 quotes a 1.48 m patch; at wind 0 the recipe's specL clamp gives 1.20 m, i.e. a FINER ring sampling (1.5 cm ~ 25.6 px, not 21 px)
scene.background_anisotropy: the windless residual keeps the existing pipeline's cos^2 lobe shape (v5 behaviour, required for the R=0 identity gate); the rain band itself is isotropic

rain.note: rate 0 == v5 behaviour exactly; the field is optional and absent in v1 recipes

recipe_v6_extension.legacy_note: v1 recipes without the rain block read exactly as before; R=0 is a hard early return to the v5 state (no band, no damping, identical omega)

rain_physics_nodes.eta_basis: impact -> ring-wave energy conversion efficiency.  The report derives everything else in the rain chain (Lambda(R), v(D), F(R), D0(R), the k band, the lifetime) but not this.  Value 0.10: about a tenth of the impact kinetic energy survives into the ring band after the cavity, crown and Worthington-jet/splash phase -- which PIPELINE-V6 section 8 explicitly excludes from the model, so that energy is lost by construction.  Order-of-magnitude calibration, NOT derived; the sensitivity is recorded in numbers-v6.json (eta 0.03/0.10/0.30).

R00.name: rain.rate_mm_h
R00.note: R=0 -> v5 behaviour exactly (no band, no damping)

placement.rule: lambda = 10mm + 10mm * (D0-D0(R=1))/(D0(R=50)-D0(R=1)); the two observed band limits are the anchors, D0(R) is the interpolation variable (report section 3.4: bigger drops -> longer rings).  Modelling placement, not a calibration.

flux.note: F_clamped is the physical variant and the gate input; F_unclamped reproduces the report table; the 0.5-5 mm band restriction gives the report's own 'factor ~2' caveat concrete

energy.note: E_flux_weighted is the mean energy per IMPACT and is what the variance budget uses

damping.weight: w(k)=1/(1+(k/310)^4) on the sub-band side only
damping.note: approximate FORM permitted by PIPELINE-V6 section 4; the magnitude is the first-order rate above, with no tuned constant.  In the windless verification scene there is nothing but the Cox-Munk floor to damp, so this is close to a no-op (recorded).

summary.physics_chain: R -> Lambda(R) -> N(D) -> v(D) -> F -> Ebar -> D0 -> k_ring -> sigma_ring^2 (eta is the only calibrated factor)

band.note: rings carry no direction: the bump is direction-uniform, in contrast to the wind spectrum's cos^2 lobe (PIPELINE-V6 section 2).  The Gaussian in k is not hard-clipped: at the extreme rates the placement sits on the band edge, so the tail crosses 310/630 (containment fraction recorded).

sigma2_breakdown.definition: sigma2 = integral k^2 S dk over the resolved band; 'calm floor' is the windless Cox-Munk-calibrated background, 'rain band' is the ring-wave contribution (PIPELINE-V6 section 7 asks for this split)

transport.method: det.py det_frame (UNCHANGED), Q=49, sigma=0.75px, no clamp / no renormalisation

crop.note: crop window chosen deterministically: the 240x240 px region where |grey(R=10)-grey(R=0)| peaks after a 48 px box average.  Row 2 is the same physical window of the C master at 1:1, so the ring grain there is not a JPEG/upscale artefact; row 1 is the literal magnification of the delivered still.

metrics_definitions.crush: fraction of pixels with rec709 linear luminance (pre-ACES, incl. exposure) < 0.02
metrics_definitions.blow: fraction of pixels with rec709 ACES luminance > 0.98 (post-ACES, pre-sRGB-encode)

display.note: same display-level normalisation as v5, evaluated once at the calm reference condition and held fixed for all R so the differences between the four stills are physical (the ring band), not exposure

gate1_backward_compatible_R0.gate: R=0 identical to the v5 baseline (C mean and stills), PIPELINE-V6 section 6 item 1

gate2_impact_flux_F.gate: F(R) integral vs report section 3.3 table, factor 1.5

gate3_ring_wavenumber.gate: k_ring(R) strictly decreasing and inside 310-630 rad/m

gate4_band_variance_monotone.gate: ring-band variance strictly increasing with R (PIPELINE-V6 section 6 item 4)

gate5_energy_and_tone.gate: mean(C)=1 (1e-3) for every master; crush/blow not implausibly worse than the v5 baseline (PIPELINE-V6 section 6 item 5)

limits.rule: crush <= max(1.5x v5-calm crush, v5-calm crush + 0.02) and blow <= v5-calm blow + 0.002; the v5 design reference 7.9% crush is recorded in crush_rows for context

gate6_single_calibration_constant.gate: the only non-derived constant of this chunk is eta (PIPELINE-V6 section 6 item 6)
gate6_single_calibration_constant.name: RING_ETA (v6_physics.RING_ETA)
gate6_single_calibration_constant.role: sigma_ring^2 = eta * F(R) * Ebar(R) * tau / (rho g + sigma k_ring^2)
gate6_single_calibration_constant.basis: impact -> ring-wave energy conversion efficiency.  The report derives everything else in the rain chain (Lambda(R), v(D), F(R), D0(R), the k band, the lifetime) but not this.  Value 0.10: about a tenth of the impact kinetic energy survives into the ring band after the cavity, crown and Worthington-jet/splash phase -- which PIPELINE-V6 section 8 explicitly excludes from the model, so that energy is lost by construction.  Order-of-magnitude calibration, NOT derived; the sensitivity is recorded in numbers-v6.json (eta 0.03/0.10/0.30).
derived_quantities: k_ring(R) (monotone placement from D0, anchored to the observed 1-2 cm band)
gate6_single_calibration_constant.not_calibrated_here: no other fitted number is introduced in chunk 2.  The inherited v5 calibrations (turbidity scale, scattering-blur proportionality, b_w(550) anchor, display-level normalisation) are unchanged and listed under inherited_calibrations_v5.

approximations_and_design_choices.statement: report 3.4 gives the observed 1-2 cm ring band and the monotone 'bigger drops -> longer rings' behaviour, but no closed-form frequency law.  The placement used is lambda = 10 mm + 10 mm * (D0-D0(R=1))/(D0(R=50)-D0(R=1)): the two observed band limits are the anchors and D0(R) is the interpolation variable.  It reproduces k(10 mm/h) = 422 rad/m vs the design's ~420.  Modelling choice, not a calibration constant.

E/(rho g + sigma k^2) converts an energy per unit area into a height variance using the deep-water linear energy density; evaluated at k_ring (the band is narrow, so this is a band-centre approximation).
tau = 150 ms is the impact-process duration measured in report 3.4, used as the mean ring lifetime as the design instructs; viscous decay is folded into it (no separate beta).

PIPELINE-V6 section 4 asks only for the mechanism with a coefficient close to 1 and the shape documented as an approximation.  gamma = F*Ebar/(rho g m0_lowk) is a first-order rate with NO tuned constant; the factor 1/(1+gamma*tau) is evaluated over one impact-process lifetime and weighted to the sub-band side only.  In this windless scene there is only the Cox-Munk floor to damp, so the applied gain is 0.998/0.987/0.926 at R=2/10/50 -- close to 1, as designed.  The per-8 s-loop value of the same rate (exp(-gamma*8)) is recorded but NOT applied: a static-spectrum loop is not the place to integrate a slow damping law.

the bump is a Gaussian in k with sigma_k = (630-310)/6; at R=1 and R=50 the centre sits on the band edge, so the tail crosses 310/630.  The variance fraction inside the band is recorded per rate (0.89 at R=2, 0.99 at R=10, 0.59 at R=50).  The bump MEAN wavenumber equals k_ring(R) by symmetry of the Gaussian, so the monotone-centre gate is exact.

approximations_and_design_choices.item: rain does not modify the light path
approximations_and_design_choices.statement: PIPELINE-V6 section 8: no airborne drops, no splash/crown/stalk geometry, no per-drop simulation.  Only the surface spectrum changes.
